questions.q: A compound with molecular formula <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> in converted by the action of acetyl chloride to a compound of molecular mass 190. The original compound <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> has how many <math><mo>-</mo><mtext>OH</mtext></math> groups?
questions.solution:
In acetylation, replacement of H of O-H occurs by CH3CO- group. -O-H+ClC||O-CH3→-OCOCH3+HCl

i.e., H atom of mass 1 amu is lost and an acetyl group of mass 43 amu is added. Thus, there is a net gain of 43 - 1 = 42 amu for every acetyl group introduced. Mass of difference of final product and original compound is 190 - 106 = 84.

Hence, number of -OH groups =8442=2 .
